Kubernetes ReplicaSets

Keep exactly N identical Pods running — the self-healing engine under every Deployment. Built around one real workload: menu-api in jahez-prod on EKS me-central-1.

apps/v1replicaset controllerselector · template · replicasownerReferencesCKADv3

Part I · High Level

What a ReplicaSet is, why it exists, and how it works inside the cluster.

1

Foundations

Definition, the problem it solves, the solution, and how it compares.

1.1Introduction

In one sentence

A ReplicaSet is a Kubernetes object that keeps a fixed number of identical Pods running — if one dies it makes another, if there are too many it removes some.

Definition. ReplicaSet is a built-in workload API (apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: ReplicaSet), stable since Kubernetes 1.9 and maintained by Kubernetes SIG Apps. You describe three things — how many Pods (replicas), which Pods count (selector) and what a new Pod looks like (template). The replicaset controller, one of the loops inside kube-controller-manager on the control plane (on EKS, AWS runs it for you), watches the object and its Pods and creates or deletes Pods until the count matches. It replaced the older ReplicationController. In day-to-day work you rarely write one: a Deployment creates one ReplicaSet per version of your Pod template and scales them for rolling updates.

✓ It is
  • A counter with a controller: “keep exactly N Pods that match this selector”.
  • The self-healing engine under every Deployment — menu-api-deployment runs its Pods through ReplicaSets.
  • Namespaced; it owns its Pods through ownerReferences, so deleting it deletes them (by default).
  • Scalable through the scale subresource — kubectl scale and the HPA both work.
✕ It is not
  • An update tool: changing the image does not touch running Pods; no rolling update, no rollback (that is a Deployment).
  • A scheduler: kube-scheduler picks the node. A load balancer: the Service sends traffic.
  • A content checker: it counts Pods by labels; it never compares their image or env with the template.
  • The tool for one Pod per node (DaemonSet), stable identity / disks (StatefulSet) or run to completion (Job).

Definitions

①

ReplicaSet

The object you write: a desired count, a label selector and a Pod template.
🎯 Why it exists

A single Pod is never re-created when it or its node dies. Something must keep watching and replace it.

📄 What it looks like
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
spec:
  replicas: 3
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

The API server stores it in etcd; the replicaset controller reads it and makes the Pods.

Before
ReplicaSet saved
Pods: 0
→
After
Pods: 3 (…-x7k2j, …-m9p4r, …-a3b8n)
📍 Where it lives

API object in etcd, namespace jahez-prod. The file lives in git at k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml.

⚠ Watch out

Created directly, it cannot roll out a new image. In production let a Deployment own it.

②

replicas

The desired number of Pods. The only field whose change acts at once.
🎯 Why it exists

Traffic changes — iftar peak vs 4 a.m. One number is easier than copying Pod files.

📄 What it looks like
spec:
  replicas: 3
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

The controller compares it with the count of matching, non-terminating Pods and creates or deletes the difference.

Before
replicas: 3 · Pods: 3
→
After
replicas: 5 · Pods: 5 (2 new)
📍 Where it lives

spec.replicas; also exposed as the /scale subresource used by kubectl scale and the HPA.

⚠ Watch out

kubectl scale changes only the live object. The next kubectl apply from git puts the old number back.

③

selector

The label query that decides which Pods the ReplicaSet counts as its own.
🎯 Why it exists

The controller needs a cheap way to find “my Pods” among thousands in the namespace.

📄 What it looks like
selector:
  matchLabels:
    app: menu-api
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

Every sync it lists Pods matching the selector, adopts orphans that match and releases owned Pods that no longer match.

Before
Pod label app=menu-api
→
After
Pod label app=menu-api-debug → released, replaced
📍 Where it lives

spec.selector (matchLabels and/or matchExpressions).

⚠ Watch out

Immutable after create. Two ReplicaSets with overlapping selectors fight over Pods — keep labels unique per app.

④

Pod template

The blueprint for every new Pod: labels plus a full Pod spec.
🎯 Why it exists

All replicas must be identical, so they are stamped from one description.

📄 What it looks like
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: menu-api
  spec:
    containers:
      - image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

Used only when a Pod is created. Existing Pods are never compared with it or changed.

Before
template image 1.25.0
Pods run 1.25.0
→
After
template image 1.26.0
Pods still run 1.25.0
📍 Where it lives

spec.template. Its labels must satisfy the selector, and restartPolicy must be Always.

⚠ Watch out

Editing the image creates mixed versions as Pods are replaced one by one. Use a Deployment for updates.

⑤

replicaset controller

The control loop that turns the object into Pods.
🎯 Why it exists

An object in etcd does nothing by itself; a controller must act on it.

📄 What it looks like
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

Reacts to watch events (Pod added, changed, deleted; ReplicaSet changed), counts, compares, then creates Pods in batches of 1, 2, 4, 8… or deletes the lowest-ranked ones.

Before
desired 3 · actual 2
→
After
POST 1 Pod → actual 3
📍 Where it lives

Inside kube-controller-manager on the EKS control plane — not on your nodes.

⚠ Watch out

It is event-driven, not a 5-second poll. A full resync happens only every 12–24 hours as a safety net.

⑥

ownerReferences

A link on each Pod that names its owning ReplicaSet.
🎯 Why it exists

The garbage collector needs to know what to delete when the owner goes, and two controllers must not both manage one Pod.

📄 What it looks like
ownerReferences:
  - kind: ReplicaSet
    name: menu-api-replica-set
    controller: true
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

Written by the controller when it creates or adopts a Pod; removed when it releases one.

Before
Pod with no owner
→
After
Pod owned by menu-api-replica-set
📍 Where it lives

metadata.ownerReferences of every Pod.

⚠ Watch out

A Pod already owned by another controller is never adopted, even if its labels match.

⑦

Adoption & orphans

An orphan is a Pod with no controller owner. Adoption is the controller claiming a matching orphan.
🎯 Why it exists

It lets you delete a ReplicaSet without killing Pods, then hand the Pods to a new one.

📄 What it looks like
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

Every sync, matching orphans get an ownerReference and are counted. If there are now too many, the extras are deleted.

Before
ReplicaSet deleted --cascade=orphan
3 orphan Pods
→
After
new ReplicaSet created
3 Pods adopted, 0 created
📍 Where it lives

Only in the ownerReferences field — there is no separate object.

⚠ Watch out

A hand-made Pod with app=menu-api is adopted too — even with the wrong image.

⑧

pod-deletion-cost

An annotation that hints which Pod to remove first when scaling down.
🎯 Why it exists

Some Pods are more expensive to lose (warm cache, long connections).

📄 What it looks like
metadata:
  annotations:
    controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost: "1000"
⚙ What Kubernetes does with it

Used as rule ④ of the scale-down ranking — after unscheduled, pending and not-ready Pods.

Before
all Pods cost 0 → newest goes
→
After
one Pod cost -100 → it goes first
📍 Where it lives

metadata.annotations of the Pod (not the ReplicaSet). Integer in the int32 range, default 0.

⚠ Watch out

Best effort and only relative between sibling Pods. The same cost on every Pod (set in the template) changes nothing.

1.2Problems or needs

In one sentence

Before ReplicaSets, every menu-api Pod was a file you applied by hand — nothing watched it, nothing replaced it, and scaling meant copying files.

Step 1 of 6 · Run menu-api as one Pod
Where① git → ② your laptop → ④ node-1WhoyouCommandkubectl apply -f
  • The catalog team ships menu-api as a single Pod file: before/menu-api-pod.yaml.
  • kube-scheduler puts it on node-1 (me-central-1a). The menu loads. Everything looks fine.
  • Nothing in the cluster knows this Pod should keep running — it is just one object.

Step 4 of 6 · Iftar peak: copy the file 5 times
Where① git · ② laptopWhoyouCommandsed + kubectl apply
  • Ramadan iftar traffic needs 5 copies. Pod names must be unique, so you generate five files.
  • Each copy is a separate object: change the image later and you must edit all five.
  • Spreading them over zones is up to you.
⎈ Full cluster · Before ReplicaSet — copy pods
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: git repo → kubectl / CI → kube-apiserver → menu-api-pod-1 → menu-api-pod-2 → menu-api-pod-5 → menu-api-pod-3 → menu-api-pod-4

for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  sed "s/name: menu-api-pod$/name: menu-api-pod-$i/" before/menu-api-pod.yaml > before/menu-api-pod-$i.yaml
  kubectl apply -f before/menu-api-pod-$i.yaml
done

Step 5 of 6 · Scale down and lose track
Where② laptop · ④ nodesWhoyouCommandkubectl delete pod
  • After the peak you delete copies one by one. Someone else had made menu-api-pod-6 with an old image last week.
  • Nobody owns these Pods, so nothing tells you how many there should be or which are stale.
  • The Service sends traffic to every Pod with app=menu-api — including the forgotten one.

Each row is solved by one object with a count, a selector and a template → 1.3 Solution.

1.3Solution

In one sentence

Write one ReplicaSet with a count, a selector and a template; the replicaset controller then creates, replaces and removes Pods to keep that count — forever.

  1. Write one file — k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml with replicas: 3, selector: app=menu-api and a Pod template.
  2. Apply it once — Argo CD (or you) sends it to kube-apiserver, which validates it (template labels must match the selector) and stores it in etcd.
  3. The controller counts — the replicaset controller sees the new object, lists Pods with app=menu-api: 0 found, 3 wanted.
  4. It creates the difference — 3 Pods named menu-api-replica-set-<5 chars>, each with an ownerReference to the ReplicaSet, created in slow-start batches (1, then 2).
  5. Scheduler and kubelet do the rest — each Pod is bound to a node, the image is pulled from ghcr.io/jahez, the readiness probe passes.
  6. It keeps watching — a Pod dies → an event → count 2 < 3 → one new Pod. You scale to 5 → two more. To 2 → three are removed by rank.
  7. The Service follows labels — menu-api-service selects app=menu-api, so new Pods get traffic as soon as they are ready.

One file per environment

Namespacejahez-dev
replicas1
CPU request100m
Whyone Pod is enough; cheap
📄 k8s/menu-api/dev/replica-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/dev/replica-set.yaml — dev
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-dev
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 1
  # ② Which Pods are mine?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
kubectl apply -f k8s/menu-api/dev/replica-set.yaml
kubectl get rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-dev
Namespacejahez-staging
replicas2
CPU request250m
Whytwo Pods test the Service spread

How each problem from 1.2 disappears

Problem in 1.2What the ReplicaSet doesField / mechanism
Node dies, Pod never comes backSees the Pod deleted, count 2 < 3, creates one on a healthy nodereconcile loop · replicas
Re-creating by hand at 2 a.m.No human step — replacement starts within seconds of the eventwatch events · slow-start create
Five copied files for iftarOne number: replicas: 5 or an HPAspec.replicas · /scale
Copies drift apartEvery new Pod comes from one templatespec.template
Forgotten stale PodsMatching orphans are adopted and counted; extras are deletedselector · adoption
Nothing for an HPA to scaleThe HPA targets the ReplicaSet scale subresourcescaleTargetRef
⚠ Watch out

Image updates are still not solved: a ReplicaSet never replaces running Pods when the template changes. That is the Deployment’s job — see 1.4 and 5.1.

1.4Comparisons

In one sentence

A ReplicaSet keeps N identical, interchangeable Pods. Use a Deployment on top of it for anything that changes over time; pick another controller when Pods need identity, one-per-node, or to finish.

Bare PodReplicationControllerReplicaSetDeploymentStatefulSetDaemonSetJob
APIv1v1 · legacyapps/v1apps/v1apps/v1apps/v1batch/v1
Keeps N PodsNoYesYesYes (via ReplicaSets)Yes, orderedOne per matching nodeUntil N succeed
Selector—Equality onlyEquality + set-basedSame as RSSame as RSSame as RSAuto-generated
Rolling update—No (old kubectl only)No — new Pods onlyYES RollingUpdate / RecreateYes, orderedYes—
Rollback—NoNoYes — revision historyYes (ControllerRevision)Yes—
Pod identityFixed nameRandom suffixRandom suffixRandom suffixStable: -0, -1 + own PVCOne per nodeRandom suffix
Typical use at JahezDebug PodNone — do not useCreated by Deploymentsmenu-api, orders-apiorders-db, RedisFluent Bit, node-exporterDB migrations
Write it yourself?RarelyNeverRarely — for learning, CKAD, custom controllersAlways for stateless appsFor statefulFor node agentsFor batch

Two ways in, one engine

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — two lanes
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-deployment → menu-api-replica-set → controller-manager → replicaset controller → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

A Deployment names its ReplicaSets menu-api-deployment-<pod-template-hash> and adds the pod-template-hash label to the selector, so old and new versions never overlap. Everything in this guide about counting, adoption and scale-down applies to those ReplicaSets too.

When to choose something else

You need…ChooseWhy not a ReplicaSet
Zero-downtime image or config changeDeploymentA ReplicaSet never replaces running Pods
Roll back to last week’s versionDeploymentA ReplicaSet keeps no history
Stable names and one disk per PodStatefulSetPods get random names and share nothing
Exactly one Pod on every nodeDaemonSetA ReplicaSet places by count, not per node
Run until done, then stopJob / CronJobrestartPolicy must be Always
Your own controller managing PodsReplicaSet (owned by your CR)✓ the right tool — like Argo Rollouts does
ⓘ ReplicationController

The original controller (v1). Still served by the API for compatibility, but its docs say to use a Deployment. Its selector is equality-only and the old kubectl rolling-update for it was removed in kubectl 1.18.

2

Architecture and workflows

Where each part runs, the repository, the controller pipeline and four traced journeys.

2.1Architecture

In one sentence

A ReplicaSet is data in etcd; the work is done by four processes — the API server stores it, the replicaset controller decides, the scheduler places, the kubelet runs.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — architecture
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: git repo → kubectl / CI → kube-apiserver → etcd → replicaset controller → kube-scheduler → kubelet node-1 → kubelet node-2 → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

PartWhere it runsWhat it does for a ReplicaSetIf it is down
kube-apiserverEKS control plane (AWS)Validates (selector ↔ labels, restartPolicy), runs admission (quota), stores, serves watchesNo changes possible; running Pods keep running
etcdEKS control planeHolds the ReplicaSet, its Pods and EventsSame as above
replicaset controllerkube-controller-managerCounts matching Pods, adopts/releases, creates or deletes, writes statusDead Pods are not replaced
garbage collectorkube-controller-managerDeletes owned Pods when the ReplicaSet is deleted (or orphans them)Deleted ReplicaSets leave Pods behind
kube-schedulerEKS control planeBinds each new Pod to a node (respects topology spread)New Pods stay Pending
kubeletevery nodePulls ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api, starts containers, runs probes, reports ReadyPods on that node go Unknown, later replaced
HPA controllerkube-controller-managerWrites /scale of the ReplicaSet from metrics-server CPUCount stays where it is
🛵 At Jahez

On EKS you never see kube-controller-manager as a Pod — AWS runs it. You see its work in Events: From: replicaset-controller.

filereplica-set.yaml
In one sentence

The ReplicaSet itself: ① how many, ② which Pods, ③ what they look like, ④ when they are available.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — replica-set.yaml
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: git repo → kubectl / CI → menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

📄 k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml — every field a ReplicaSet has
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    team: catalog
  annotations:
    jahez.net/owner: catalog-team
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3                          # desired count; the controller keeps exactly this many
  # ② Which Pods are mine?  (immutable after create)
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
    matchExpressions:
      - key: tier
        operator: In
        values: ["api"]
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:                          # must satisfy the selector above
        app: menu-api
        tier: api
        version: "1.25.0"              # not in the selector, so it may change
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "8080"
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always            # the only value a ReplicaSet accepts
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
              value: Production
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/live
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: menu-api
  # ④ When does a new Pod count as available?
  minReadySeconds: 10                  # ready for 10 s without a crash
What each block does
① replicas
desired count
② selector
label query, immutable
③ template
blueprint for new Pods only
④ minReadySeconds
ready time before “available”

# k8s/menu-api/hpa.yaml — let CPU decide spec.replicas (3 to 10)
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: menu-api-hpa
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① What does it scale?
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: ReplicaSet
    name: menu-api-replica-set
  # ② Between which limits?
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  # ③ On which signal?
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 70

fileprometheus-rule.yaml
In one sentence

Alerts when the ReplicaSet cannot reach or keep its desired count.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — prometheus-rule.yaml
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: git repo → menu-api-prometheus-rule → kube-state-metrics → Prometheus

📄 k8s/menu-api/prometheus-rule.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/prometheus-rule.yaml — alert when the ReplicaSet cannot keep its count
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: menu-api-prometheus-rule
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
spec:
  groups:
    - name: menu-api.replicaset
      rules:
        # ① Fewer Pods exist than desired
        - alert: MenuApiReplicasMismatch
          expr: |
            kube_replicaset_spec_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
              != kube_replicaset_status_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: warning
          annotations:
            summary: "menu-api-replica-set has not reached its desired count for 5 minutes"
        # ② Pods exist but are not ready
        - alert: MenuApiReplicasNotReady
          expr: |
            kube_replicaset_status_ready_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
              < kube_replicaset_spec_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
          annotations:
            summary: "menu-api has fewer ready Pods than desired — check readiness probes and Events"
What each block does
① Mismatch
spec ≠ status for 5 min — quota, scheduling, image pull
② NotReady
Pods exist but readiness fails

2.3The reconcile loop

In one sentence

Each time something about a ReplicaSet or its Pods changes, the controller runs one sync: list matching Pods → adopt or release → compare with replicas → create or delete the difference → write status.

✕ Correction

The old guide said the loop runs “every ~5 seconds”. It does not poll: it is driven by watch events. A full resync only happens every 12–24 hours as a safety net.

Example traced below: menu-api-replica-set wants 3; Pod …-m9p4r just crashed out of node-1 (OOM, evicted). Every input row opens the object in a popup.

Step 1 of 7 · Trigger
Stage0 · TriggerWherenode-1 · API serverField—
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — stage 0
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kubectl / CI → kubelet node-1 → kube-apiserver

What happens. kubelet on node-1 reports that …-m9p4r was OOM-killed and evicted; the Pod object is deleted. Any of these also trigger a sync: a Pod added, a label edited, replicas changed, the ReplicaSet created.

① INPUTwhat reaches this stage
CMDwhat happened
DELETE pod menu-api-replica-set-m9p4r   # by kubelet eviction
# or: kubectl scale rs menu-api-replica-set --replicas=5
# or: kubectl label pod … app-
② LOGICthe field that drives it

No field yet — the trigger is any change to the ReplicaSet or a Pod it could own.

③ OUTPUT RAM → etcdwhat it produces
⚡DELETE event for Pod m9p4rNEW
📌 Remember

Deleting a Pod is the fastest way to see self-healing — the replacement starts within a second or two.

Step 2 of 7 · Watch event
Stage1 · Watch eventWherekube-controller-managerFieldownerReferences
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — stage 1
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kube-apiserver → replicaset controller

What happens. The controller’s Pod informer receives the DELETE, finds the owner from ownerReferences and queues the key jahez-prod/menu-api-replica-set. It also lowers its “expectations” so it stops waiting for that delete.

① INPUTwhat reaches this stage
CACHEinformer cache · from the API server watch
② LOGICthe field that drives it

metadata.ownerReferences of the Pod → which ReplicaSet to sync.

③ OUTPUT RAM → etcdwhat it produces
📥queue: jahez-prod/menu-api-replica-setNEW
📌 Remember

Many events for the same ReplicaSet collapse into one queued key — one sync handles them all.

Step 3 of 7 · List by selector
Stage2 · List by selectorWherekube-controller-managerFieldselector
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — stage 2
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: replicaset controller → menu-api-replica-set → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…a3b8n → menu-api-stray-pod

What happens. The sync lists every Pod in jahez-prod whose labels match spec.selector, from the local cache (no API call). It drops Pods that are Succeeded, Failed or already terminating.

① INPUTwhat reaches this stage
CACHEcache · Pods in jahez-prod
② LOGICthe field that drives it
📄 replica-set.yamlyaml
selector:
  matchLabels:
    app: menu-api

Only app=menu-api Pods pass. orders-api is ignored.

③ OUTPUT RAM → etcdwhat it produces
◆x7k2jUNCHANGED
◆a3b8nUNCHANGED
◆stray-pod (orphan)NEW
📌 Remember

Terminating Pods are not counted — the replacement can start before the old Pod is fully gone.

Step 4 of 7 · Adopt / release
Stage3 · Adopt / releaseWherekube-controller-managerFieldownerReferences
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — stage 3
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: replicaset controller → garbage collector → Pod objects

What happens. Matching Pods with no controller owner are adopted (an ownerReference is patched in). Owned Pods that no longer match are released (ownerReference removed). Pods owned by another controller are skipped.

① INPUTwhat reaches this stage
CACHEfrom stage 2
② LOGICthe field that drives it

ownerReferences[].controller — at most one controller owner per Pod.

③ OUTPUT RAM → etcdwhat it produces
◆stray-pod → owner menu-api-replica-setADOPTED
📌 Remember

The stray Pod runs image 1.24.0. The ReplicaSet adopts it anyway — it never checks the image.

Step 5 of 7 · Compare

Step 6 of 7 · Create / delete
Stage5 · Create / deleteWherekube-controller-managerFieldtemplate

Lit: replicaset controller → kube-apiserver → kube-scheduler → menu-api-…p4r5t

What happens. If diff < 0 the controller creates Pods from spec.template in slow-start batches 1, 2, 4, 8… (max 500 per sync); if one batch fails it stops. If diff > 0 it ranks Pods and deletes the lowest — see 5.3. Below: the case without the stray Pod.

=diff = 2 − 3 = −1CHANGED

spec:

      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0

📌 Remember

Creates can be refused (quota, admission) — the error lands in Events and in a ReplicaFailure condition.

Part II · Low Level — details and depth

Every field, every relationship with Pods, every operation and every command.

3

The ReplicaSet object

Four questions, every field, and what Kubernetes writes back.

3.0How a ReplicaSet works

In one sentence

A ReplicaSet answers four questions — how many, which Pods, what new Pods look like, when they count as available — and Kubernetes writes the answers back in status.

Think of it as a thermostat for Pods: you set the number, the controller measures the room (Pods matching the selector) and switches Pods on or off. It lives until you delete it; its Pods live and die many times under it.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
① How many Pods?replicasthe thermostat setting
② Which Pods are mine?selector (immutable)the name tag the controller looks for
③ What does each new Pod look like?templatea cookie cutter — used only for new Pods
④ When does a new Pod count as available?minReadySecondsa probation period after Ready
Written by Kubernetesstatus, generation, Pod ownerReferencesthe meter reading
Familyworkload · apps/v1
Scopenamespaced
Short namers
Survivesuntil deleted
Typical ownera Deployment
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — how a replicaset works
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n → Pod objects

Structure

▤ structure treeoutput
ReplicaSet
├── metadata           name · namespace · labels · annotations
├── spec
│   ├── ① replicas      int (default 1)
│   ├── ② selector      matchLabels · matchExpressions      (immutable)
│   ├── ③ template
│   │   ├── metadata     labels (must satisfy selector) · annotations
│   │   └── spec         a full Pod spec · restartPolicy: Always
│   └── ④ minReadySeconds int (default 0)
└── status               replicas · fullyLabeledReplicas · readyReplicas · availableReplicas · observedGeneration · conditions
📄 k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml — every field a ReplicaSet has
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    team: catalog
  annotations:
    jahez.net/owner: catalog-team
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3                          # desired count; the controller keeps exactly this many
  # ② Which Pods are mine?  (immutable after create)
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
    matchExpressions:
      - key: tier
        operator: In
        values: ["api"]
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:                          # must satisfy the selector above
        app: menu-api
        tier: api
        version: "1.25.0"              # not in the selector, so it may change
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "8080"
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always            # the only value a ReplicaSet accepts
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
              value: Production
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/live
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: menu-api
  # ④ When does a new Pod count as available?
  minReadySeconds: 10                  # ready for 10 s without a crash

🌳 menu-api-replica-set — every property
· metadatagroupidentity of the ReplicaSet itself
• namestringrequiredends with -replica-set; Pods are named <name>-<5 chars>
namespacestringPods are created in the same namespace

Default: default

labelsobjectlabels on the ReplicaSet (not on its Pods)

Changing them takes effect at once and changes nothing about Pods. Do not confuse with spec.template.metadata.labels.

• annotationsobjectfree-form notes, e.g. owner team
① How many Pods?groupthe desired count
replicasintegerdesired number of Pods

The only field whose change acts at once. Exposed as the /scale subresource.

ValueMeaning
0keep the ReplicaSet, delete all Pods
1default when omitted
3menu-api in prod
10HPA max at iftar

Default: 1

Deep dive →
② Which Pods are mine?grouplabel query · immutable
selectorobjectrequiredwhich Pods the controller counts

Immutable after create. Must be satisfied by the template labels. An empty selector is rejected in apps/v1.

Deep dive →
• matchLabelsobjectkey=value pairs, all must match (AND)
matchExpressionslistset-based rules, all must match (AND)
• keystringrequiredlabel key
operatorstringrequiredIn · NotIn · Exists · DoesNotExist
ValueMeaning
Invalue in the list
NotInvalue not in the list, or key absent
Existskey present
DoesNotExistkey absent
• valueslistneeded for In/NotIn; must be empty for Exists/DoesNotExist
③ What does each new Pod look like?groupthe Pod template
templateobjectrequiredblueprint for new Pods only

Changing it never touches running Pods.

Deep dive →
metadata.labelsobjectrequiredmust satisfy spec.selector

Otherwise: `selector` does not match template `labels`. Extra labels are fine.

• metadata.annotationsobjectcopied onto each Pod
spec.restartPolicystringonly Always is accepted

Default: Always

• spec.containerslistrequiredimage, ports, env, resources, probes — as in any Pod
• spec.topologySpreadConstraintslistspread replicas over zones (the scheduler applies it)
spec.terminationGracePeriodSecondsintegertime to finish requests after SIGTERM on scale-down

Default: 30

④ When does a new Pod count as available?groupprobation after Ready
minReadySecondsintegerseconds a Pod must stay Ready before it is available

Default: 0

Written by Kubernetesgroupdo not set these
• status.replicasintegermatching, non-terminating Pods
• status.readyReplicasintegerPods passing readiness
• status.availableReplicasintegerready for ≥ minReadySeconds
• status.fullyLabeledReplicasintegerPods with every template label
• status.observedGenerationintegerwhich spec version status describes
status.conditionslistReplicaFailure when Pods cannot be created

3.1① replicas

In one sentence

replicas is the desired number of Pods; change it and the controller creates or deletes the difference within seconds.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — replicas flow
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kubectl / CI → HPA controller → git repo → menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…k2j7n → menu-api-…p4r5t

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as

📄 k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml — ① How many Pods?
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3                  # 0 is allowed: keeps the ReplicaSet, removes every Pod
  # ② Which Pods are mine?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0

kind: ReplicaSet

spec:

  selector:

Immutable — what happens if you try

# change matchLabels app: menu-api → app: menu  in the file, then:
kubectl apply -f k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml
▤ example outputoutput
The ReplicaSet "menu-api-replica-set" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: v1.LabelSelector{MatchLabels:map[string]string{"app":"menu"}, MatchExpressions:[]v1.LabelSelectorRequirement(nil)}: field is immutable
✓ The way around it

To change a selector: kubectl delete rs menu-api-replica-set --cascade=orphan, edit the file, apply again — the new ReplicaSet adopts the existing Pods if their labels match the new selector.

⚠ Watch out

Two ReplicaSets whose selectors overlap (e.g. both app=menu-api) do not share Pods — each owns what it created — but each also adopts any orphan that matches, and a Service with the same selector mixes them. Keep one unique label set per app; a Deployment adds pod-template-hash for exactly this reason.

3.3③ template

In one sentence

The template is the blueprint for every new Pod; it is read only when a Pod is created, so editing it never changes running Pods.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — template flow
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…p4r5t → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…a3b8n

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
③ What does each new Pod look like?template.metadata · template.speca cookie cutter: shapes new cookies, not baked ones
📄 k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml — ③ the Pod template
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    # ── Pod metadata ──
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api                  # required: must satisfy spec.selector
        version: "1.25.0"              # extra labels are fine
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
    # ── Pod spec — the same fields as a normal Pod ──
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always            # OnFailure / Never are rejected
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: http

3.4④ minReadySeconds

In one sentence

minReadySeconds makes a new Pod wait a little after it becomes Ready before it is counted as available.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — minready flow
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kubelet node-2 → menu-api-…p4r5t → replicaset controller → menu-api-replica-set

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
④ When does a new Pod count as available?minReadySecondsa probation period after Ready
📄 k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml — ④ minReadySeconds
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: 8080
            periodSeconds: 5
  # ④ When does a new Pod count as available?
  minReadySeconds: 10          # ready → wait 10 s → available

ⓘ Where it matters

On a bare ReplicaSet it only changes status.availableReplicas (which alerts and PDBs read). Its real job is in a Deployment: a rolling update waits for available, so a Pod that crashes after 5 s stops the rollout.

apiVersion: v1

  labels:
    app: menu-api
    tier: api
  ownerReferences:                        # written by the replicaset controller
    - apiVersion: apps/v1

      uid: 6f1c2b7e-3d4a-4f58-9a61-0b2e8c4d7a11

      blockOwnerDeletion: true            # foreground delete waits for this Pod
spec:
  nodeName: ip-192-168-1-101.me-central-1.compute.internal
  containers:
    - name: menu-api
      image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
ⓘ pod-template-hash

If a Deployment created the ReplicaSet, both carry a pod-template-hash label and the selector includes it. A ReplicaSet you write yourself has no such label.

4

Pods and ownership

How the ReplicaSet decides which Pods are its own, and how to influence it.

4.1Ownership & adoption

In one sentence

A Pod belongs to the ReplicaSet named in its ownerReferences; matching orphans are adopted, owned Pods that stop matching are released.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — ownership flow
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-stray-pod → replicaset controller → Pod objects

📄 kubectl get pod menu-api-replica-set-x7k2j -o yamlyaml
# kubectl get pod menu-api-replica-set-x7k2j -n jahez-prod -o yaml — the owner link
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set-x7k2j       # <ReplicaSet name>-<5 random chars>
  generateName: menu-api-replica-set-
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    tier: api
  ownerReferences:                        # written by the replicaset controller
    - apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: ReplicaSet
      name: menu-api-replica-set
      uid: 6f1c2b7e-3d4a-4f58-9a61-0b2e8c4d7a11
      controller: true                    # this owner is THE controller (only one allowed)
      blockOwnerDeletion: true            # foreground delete waits for this Pod
spec:
  nodeName: ip-192-168-1-101.me-central-1.compute.internal
  containers:
    - name: menu-api
      image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0

A Pod of menu-api-deployment carries app=menu-api too.

📄 file appliedyaml
# k8s/menu-api/deployment.yaml — the production way: a Deployment that owns ReplicaSets
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3
  # ② Which Pods are mine?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: 8080
  # ④ How do changes roll out?  (a ReplicaSet has no such field)
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
kubectl get pods -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,OWNER:.metadata.ownerReferences[0].name

4.2Isolating a Pod

In one sentence

Change one label on a misbehaving Pod and the ReplicaSet lets it go and starts a replacement — the old Pod keeps running for you to debug.

Change the valuekubectl label pod X app=menu-api-debug --overwriteOut of Service and RS; easy to find later

⚠ Watch out

Do not forget the isolated Pod — it has no owner, so nothing will ever delete it. Delete it when you are done.

4.3Pod deletion cost

In one sentence

The controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost annotation on a Pod tells the controller which siblings to remove first when scaling down — lower cost goes first.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — deletion cost flow
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n → replicaset controller

✕ Correction

Corrected from the old guide: a cost of 500 or 1000 does not “protect” a Pod. Costs only matter compared with sibling Pods of the same ReplicaSet, the rule is best effort, values must fit in an int32 (−2147483648 … 2147483647), and putting one cost in the template gives every Pod the same value — no effect.

Question it answersFieldsThink of it as
Which Pod should go first?metadata.annotations["controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost"]a sticky note: “cheap to lose” / “expensive to lose”
📄 k8s/menu-api/pod-deletion-cost-high.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/pod-deletion-cost-high.yaml — protect a warm-cache Pod
# Normally you annotate the live Pod (kubectl annotate). This shows the same thing as YAML.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set-x7k2j
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    tier: api
  annotations:
    # ① How costly is it to delete this Pod?
    controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost: "1000"   # higher than its siblings → deleted later
spec:
  containers:
    - name: menu-api
      image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
📄 k8s/menu-api/pod-deletion-cost-low.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/pod-deletion-cost-low.yaml — mark a degraded Pod to go first
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set-m9p4r
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    tier: api
  annotations:
    # ① How costly is it to delete this Pod?
    controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost: "-100"   # lower than its siblings → deleted earlier
spec:
  containers:
    - name: menu-api
      image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0

🌳 pod-deletion-cost — every property
controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-coststringinteger as a string, on the Pod

Read only during scale-down ranking. Writing it often (e.g. from metrics every few seconds) creates heavy API traffic — update it just before you scale down.

ValueMeaning
"-100"lower than siblings → earlier
"0"neutral
"1000"higher than siblings → later

Default: "0"

SiblingsWho goes first on 3 → 2Why
0 · 0 · 0decided by rules ⑤–⑧ (node, ready time, restarts, age)costs equal
1000 · -100 · 0the -100 Podlowest cost
500 · 500 · 500 (template)same as all 0no difference between siblings
1000 · 0 · 0 but one Pod Pendingthe Pending Podrules ①–③ come before cost
5

Operations

Updating, scaling, the scale-down ranking, deleting, and the production set.

5.1Updating the template

In one sentence

Changing the image in a ReplicaSet’s template updates nothing that is running; only Pods created afterwards use it — so updates need either manual Pod deletes (downtime risk) or a Deployment.

Step 1 of 6 · Before

All 3 Pods run menu-api:1.25.0; the template says the same.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — img before
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-replica-set → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

Step 2 of 6 · Change the template

Three ways to set 1.26.0 — all only change spec.template:

# 1 · edit the file in git (image: …:1.26.0), then
kubectl apply -f k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml

# 2 · edit the live object
kubectl edit rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod

# 3 · set image / patch
kubectl set image rs/menu-api-replica-set menu-api=ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0 -n jahez-prod
kubectl patch rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/image","value":"ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0"}]'

✕ Downtime

Every Pod stops at once: no ready endpoint until new Pods pass readiness. Deleting one Pod at a time (wait for READY between) avoids the outage but is a manual rolling update.

Step 6 of 6 · Fix B: use a Deployment
kubectl set image deployment/menu-api-deployment menu-api=ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0 -n jahez-prod
💡 Command hint
send template change→store in etcd→✕ running Pods unchanged
kubectlthe Kubernetes CLI
setchange one field by a sub-command
imageset image: change a container image
deployment/menu-api-deploymentobject name or argument
menu-api=ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0object name or argument
-nnamespace

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — fix b
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-deployment → menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…p4r5t → menu-api-…k2j7n

The Deployment creates a new ReplicaSet for the new template and moves the count across one Pod at a time; each new Pod must be available before an old one goes. Zero downtime, with kubectl rollout undo.

📄 k8s/menu-api/deployment.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/deployment.yaml — the production way: a Deployment that owns ReplicaSets
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3
  # ② Which Pods are mine?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: 8080
  # ④ How do changes roll out?  (a ReplicaSet has no such field)
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5

What can you change on a running ReplicaSet?

FieldChangeable?Takes effectHow
spec.replicas✓At oncescale · patch · edit · apply
spec.template.spec.containers[*].image✓ templateNew Pods onlyset image · patch · edit
…containers[*].env · resources · probes✓ templateNew Pods onlypatch · edit · set env · set resources
spec.template.metadata.labels✓ if still matchingNew Pods onlyedit · patch
spec.minReadySeconds✓Next status updatepatch · edit
spec.selector✕ immutable—delete --cascade=orphan, re-create
metadata.labels (of the RS)✓At oncelabel — Pods unaffected

Deep dive — update options compared

Fast, simple, outage while the new Pods start.

kubectl delete pods -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api

No outage if you wait for READY each time; slow and error-prone.

for p in $(kubectl get pods -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api -o name); do
  kubectl delete $p -n jahez-prod
  kubectl wait rs/menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --for=jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}'=3 --timeout=120s
done

Automatic, zero downtime, history and rollback.

kubectl set image deployment/menu-api-deployment menu-api=ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0 -n jahez-prod
kubectl rollout status deployment/menu-api-deployment -n jahez-prod
Delete allOne by oneDeployment
Downtime✕ yes✓ none if careful✓ none
Effortone commandscriptone command
Rollbackmanualmanualrollout undo
Jahez prod✕✕✓

5.2Scaling

In one sentence

Scaling changes only spec.replicas; it takes effect at once — more Pods from the current template, or fewer chosen by the ranking in 5.3.

Where② laptop → ③ controller → ④ nodesWhoyouCommandkubectl scale

kubectl scale rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --replicas=5
kubectl get rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod

menu-api-replica-set-a3b8n   1/1     Running       0          5m
menu-api-replica-set-x7k2j   1/1     Running       0          5m
menu-api-replica-set-m9p4r   1/1     Terminating   0          5m

The controller ranks the 5 Pods (5.3) and deletes 3. Each gets SIGTERM, then up to terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30.

kubectl scale rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --replicas=0
kubectl get rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod

NAME                   DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AGE
menu-api-replica-set   0         0         0       6h

The ReplicaSet and its template stay; all Pods go. Bring them back with --replicas=3. Useful in jahez-dev overnight.

# 1 · scale (live only)
kubectl scale rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --replicas=5

# 2 · edit git, then apply (GitOps — best)
kubectl apply -f k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml

# 3 · edit live
kubectl edit rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod

# 4 · patch
kubectl patch rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod -p '{"spec":{"replicas":5}}'

# 5 · conditional — only if it is exactly 3 now
kubectl scale rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --replicas=5 --current-replicas=3

# 6 · automatic
kubectl autoscale rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --min=3 --max=10 --cpu-percent=70

↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: git repo → kubectl / CI → menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…k2j7n → menu-api-…p4r5t

✕ Drift

You scale to 5 live; git still says 3. The next kubectl apply or Argo CD sync scales back to 3 — your extra Pods disappear at peak time. Change the file and commit, or let an HPA own the number.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — hpa
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: metrics-server → HPA controller → menu-api-hpa → menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller

📄 k8s/menu-api/hpa.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/hpa.yaml — let CPU decide spec.replicas (3 to 10)
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: menu-api-hpa
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① What does it scale?
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: ReplicaSet
    name: menu-api-replica-set
  # ② Between which limits?
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  # ③ On which signal?
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 70

5.3Scale-down ranking

In one sentence

When there are too many Pods, the controller sorts them by eight rules and deletes from the top — the least useful Pods go first.

✕ Correction

Corrected from the old guide (which listed 5 rules with “newest” before readiness): the real order checks readiness and restart count, and deletion cost comes only after scheduling, phase and readiness.

  1. Unscheduled before scheduledA Pod with no node yet is deleted first — it serves nothing.
  2. Pending before Unknown before RunningPod phase: the least useful phase goes first.
  3. Not ready before readyA Pod failing readiness gets no traffic anyway.
  4. Lower pod-deletion-cost firstThe annotation from 4.3; default 0.
  5. More replicas on the same node first“Doubled up” Pods go first, so replicas stay spread over nodes.
  6. Ready for less time firstA Pod that just became ready is less proven (compared in log-scale buckets).
  7. Higher restart count firstA Pod that keeps restarting goes before a stable one.
  8. Newer before olderCreation time, also in log-scale buckets; remaining ties are effectively random.
Step 1 of 9 · Rule 1

Unscheduled before scheduled. A Pod with no node yet is deleted first — it serves nothing.

5.4Deleting & cascade

In one sentence

Deleting a ReplicaSet deletes its Pods by default; --cascade decides whether that happens in the background, in the foreground, or not at all.

--cascadeReplicaSetPodskubectl returnsUse it for
background (default)deleted at oncedeleted after by the garbage collectorimmediatelynormal clean-up
foregroundstays (deletionTimestamp) until Pods are gonedeleted firstafter the API accepts; object visible until Pods are gonescripts that must know Pods are gone
orphandeletedkeep running, ownerReferences removedimmediatelychanging the selector, handing Pods to a new RS

--cascade=background

In one sentence

The default: the ReplicaSet disappears, then the garbage collector deletes its Pods.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — delete background
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kubectl / CI → kube-apiserver → garbage collector → kubelet node-1 → kubelet node-2 → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

kubectl delete rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod
💡 Command hint
delete the ReplicaSet→garbage collector deletes its Pods
kubectlthe Kubernetes CLI
deletedelete objects
rsshort name for replicasets
menu-api-replica-setobject name or argument
-nnamespace
jahez-prodobject name or argument

Result
All 3 Pods Terminating within a second.
✕ When it fails

Pods stuck Terminating → a finalizer on the Pod or an unreachable node.

--cascade=foreground

In one sentence

The ReplicaSet gets a foregroundDeletion finalizer; the garbage collector deletes Pods first (they have blockOwnerDeletion), then the ReplicaSet.

Result

✕ When it fails

A Pod that never terminates keeps the ReplicaSet forever.

--cascade=orphan

In one sentence

The garbage collector removes the ownerReference from each Pod, then the ReplicaSet is deleted. Pods keep serving.

5.5Production set

In one sentence

In production a ReplicaSet never travels alone: a Service gives it an address, a PDB protects it during drains, an HPA sizes it — all selecting app=menu-api.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — production set
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: git repo → menu-api-replica-set → menu-api-service → menu-api-pdb → menu-api-hpa → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

📄 k8s/menu-api/production-set.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/production-set.yaml — ReplicaSet + Service + PDB + HPA in one file
# ── 1. ReplicaSet ──
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    team: catalog
  annotations:
    jahez.net/owner: catalog-team
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3                          # desired count; the controller keeps exactly this many
  # ② Which Pods are mine?  (immutable after create)
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
    matchExpressions:
      - key: tier
        operator: In
        values: ["api"]
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:                          # must satisfy the selector above
        app: menu-api
        tier: api
        version: "1.25.0"              # not in the selector, so it may change
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: "8080"
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always            # the only value a ReplicaSet accepts
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
              value: Production
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/live
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: menu-api
  # ④ When does a new Pod count as available?
  minReadySeconds: 10                  # ready for 10 s without a crash
---
# ── 2. Service ──
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-api-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which Pods get traffic?
  selector:
    app: menu-api                      # same label the ReplicaSet stamps on its Pods
  # ② Which ports?
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
---
# ── 3. PodDisruptionBudget ──
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: menu-api-pdb
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which Pods?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ② How many must stay up during a drain?
  minAvailable: 2
---
# ── 4. HorizontalPodAutoscaler ──
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: menu-api-hpa
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① What does it scale?
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: ReplicaSet
    name: menu-api-replica-set
  # ② Between which limits?
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  # ③ On which signal?
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 70

6.7Troubleshooting

In one sentence

Every ReplicaSet failure happens at one of five stages; read the error, find the stage, apply the fix.

⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — where errors appear
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kubectl / CI → kube-apiserver → jahez-prod-resource-quota → kube-scheduler → kubelet node-1 → menu-api-…k2j7n

#SymptomError / EventFix
1apply rejectedspec.template.metadata.labels: Invalid value: …: `selector` does not match template `labels`Make template labels satisfy the selector
2apply rejectedspec.selector: Invalid value: …: field is immutabledelete --cascade=orphan, then apply
3DESIRED 3, CURRENT 2FailedCreate … is forbidden: exceeded quota: jahez-prod-resource-quotaRaise quota or lower requests; check kubectl describe quota
4Pods PendingFailedScheduling 0/2 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient cpuAdd nodes (Karpenter / node group) or lower requests
5READY 0/3Back-off pulling image "ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0" (ImagePullBackOff)Fix the tag or the imagePullSecret
6READY 2/3, restartsBack-off restarting failed container menu-api (CrashLoopBackOff)kubectl logs --previous; fix config / probes
7Pods do not match after applyapply succeeded but Pods still oldTemplate changes need new Pods (5.1)

7Labs with hidden solutions

LAB 1Create a ReplicaSet from scratch

In jahez-prod create ReplicaSet menu-api-replica-set with 3 replicas of ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0, label app=menu-api, container port 8080. No YAML is given.

🔒 Show the solution
What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — lab 1
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: kubectl / CI → kube-apiserver → menu-api-replica-set → replicaset controller → menu-api-…x7k2j → menu-api-…m9p4r → menu-api-…a3b8n

kubectl create deployment menu-api-replica-set --image=ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0 --replicas=3 --port=8080 -n jahez-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml > rs.yaml
sed -i 's/kind: Deployment/kind: ReplicaSet/; /strategy: {}/d; /status: {}/d' rs.yaml
sed -i 's/app: menu-api-replica-set/app: menu-api/' rs.yaml
kubectl create -f rs.yaml
📄 rs.yaml (cleaned)yaml
# k8s/menu-api/replica-set.yaml — the smallest working ReplicaSet
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: menu-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3
  # ② Which Pods are mine?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.25.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
Verify
kubectl get rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod
kubectl get pods -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api
▤ example outputoutput
NAME                   DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AGE
menu-api-replica-set   3         3         3       25s
Exam traps
  • kubectl create deployment labels Pods with app=<deployment name> — fix both selector and template labels.
  • Remove strategy: a ReplicaSet rejects the unknown field (strict validation).
  • There is no kubectl create replicaset.

LAB 7Move menu-api from a ReplicaSet to a Deployment

Replace menu-api-replica-set with menu-api-deployment (image 1.26.0) with no moment of zero ready Pods.

🔒 Show the solution
What you will build
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — lab 7
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-replica-set → menu-api-deployment → replicaset controller → menu-api-…p4r5t → menu-api-…k2j7n

📄 k8s/menu-api/deployment.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/deployment.yaml — the production way: a Deployment that owns ReplicaSets
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① How many Pods?
  replicas: 3
  # ② Which Pods are mine?
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  # ③ What does each new Pod look like?
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz/ready
              port: 8080
  # ④ How do changes roll out?  (a ReplicaSet has no such field)
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
kubectl apply -f k8s/menu-api/deployment.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/menu-api-deployment -n jahez-prod
kubectl get rs -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api
kubectl delete rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --ignore-not-found
ⓘ What actually happens

The old ReplicaSet has app=menu-api in its own labels and no owner, so the Deployment controller adopts it as an “old” ReplicaSet and scales it down while the new one scales up. If its labels did not match, both would run side by side until you delete the old one — the Service serves both meanwhile.

Verify
kubectl get pods -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.containers[0].image
Exam traps
  • Do not delete the old ReplicaSet first — that is a full outage.
  • Remove replica-set.yaml from the kustomization in the same commit, or Argo CD re-creates it.
8

Monitoring & practices

What to alert on and how to run ReplicaSets well.

8.1Metrics & alerts

In one sentence

Alert on the gap between desired and ready — that single signal catches quota limits, scheduling failures, image pulls and crash loops.

Metric (kube-state-metrics)MeaningAlert when
kube_replicaset_spec_replicasdesired—
kube_replicaset_status_replicasexisting matching Pods≠ desired for 5 min
kube_replicaset_status_ready_replicasready Pods< desired for 5 min
kube_replicaset_status_observed_generation vs kube_replicaset_metadata_generationcontroller caught up?differ for 5 min
kube_replicaset_ownerowner kind (Deployment / none)owner_kind="<none>" in prod
⎈ Full cluster · With ReplicaSet — monitoring
↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen

Lit: menu-api-replica-set → kube-state-metrics → Prometheus → menu-api-prometheus-rule

📄 k8s/menu-api/prometheus-rule.yamlyaml
# k8s/menu-api/prometheus-rule.yaml — alert when the ReplicaSet cannot keep its count
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: menu-api-prometheus-rule
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    release: kube-prometheus-stack
spec:
  groups:
    - name: menu-api.replicaset
      rules:
        # ① Fewer Pods exist than desired
        - alert: MenuApiReplicasMismatch
          expr: |
            kube_replicaset_spec_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
              != kube_replicaset_status_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: warning
          annotations:
            summary: "menu-api-replica-set has not reached its desired count for 5 minutes"
        # ② Pods exist but are not ready
        - alert: MenuApiReplicasNotReady
          expr: |
            kube_replicaset_status_ready_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
              < kube_replicaset_spec_replicas{namespace="jahez-prod",replicaset="menu-api-replica-set"}
          for: 5m
          labels:
            severity: critical
          annotations:
            summary: "menu-api has fewer ready Pods than desired — check readiness probes and Events"
⌘ Commands

load the rules

kubectl apply -f k8s/menu-api/prometheus-rule.yaml

kubectlthe Kubernetes CLI

-ffile, folder or URL to read

kubectl get rs -A -o custom-columns=NS:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,OWNER:.metadata.ownerReferences[0].kind

kubectlthe Kubernetes CLI

-Aall namespaces

8.2Best practices

In one sentence

Let Deployments own ReplicaSets, keep labels unique, keep git the source of truth, and always pair replicas with a PDB and spread.

Use Deployments

Never hand-create a ReplicaSet in production. Deployments add rolling updates and rollback on top of the same engine.

Unique labels

One label set per app (app=menu-api) — no overlap between selectors, no hand-made Pods with app labels.

No live scaling under GitOps

kubectl scale drifts from git. Change the file or let an HPA own replicas.

PDB + spread

From 2 replicas on, add a PodDisruptionBudget and a zone topology spread so drains and AZ failures keep capacity.

Requests set

CPU/memory requests make scheduling, quota math and the HPA work.

Readiness probe + minReadySeconds

READY and AVAILABLE only mean something if the probe checks real dependencies.

🛵 SRE wisdom

ReplicaSets are the engine of self-healing; Deployments are the steering wheel. Understand the engine to debug; drive with the wheel in production.

Template (new Pods only!)
kubectl set image rs/menu-api-replica-set menu-api=ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.26.0 -n jahez-prod
kubectl edit rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod
kubectl delete pods -n jahez-prod -l app=menu-api   # ⚠ outage: forces new Pods
Ownership
kubectl label pod menu-api-replica-set-m9p4r -n jahez-prod app=menu-api-debug --overwrite
kubectl annotate pod menu-api-replica-set-m9p4r -n jahez-prod controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost=-100 --overwrite
Delete
kubectl delete rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod
kubectl delete rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --cascade=foreground
kubectl delete rs menu-api-replica-set -n jahez-prod --cascade=orphan

Traps to remember

  • Template changes never touch running Pods.
  • The selector is immutable; template labels must satisfy it.
  • Any orphan Pod with matching labels is adopted — even with the wrong image.
  • The controller is event-driven; there is no 5-second loop.
  • Scale-down order: unscheduled → pending → not ready → cost → doubled-up → ready time → restarts → newest.
  • pod-deletion-cost is relative and best effort.
  • kubectl scale is undone by the next apply from git.
  • restartPolicy must be Always.

  generateName: menu-api-replica-set-
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
    tier: api
  ownerReferences:                        # written by the replicaset controller

      name: menu-api-replica-set

      blockOwnerDeletion: true            # foreground delete waits for this Pod

  nodeName: ip-192-168-1-101.me-central-1.compute.internal
  containers:
    - name: menu-api

# k8s/orders-api/replica-set.yaml — a second ReplicaSet with its own labels
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ReplicaSet
metadata:
  name: orders-api-replica-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  replicas: 2
  # ② Which Pods are mine?  (no overlap with menu-api)
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: orders-api
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: orders-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/orders-api:3.8.2
